reason: gpu-pinning-broken-by-early-cuInit (all 3 phase1 cells co-located on physical GPU 0 -> CUDA OOM at the first probe-callback read, ~step 4)

Root cause (diagnosed empirically on pod-543): the dispatcher's import chain calls cuInit BEFORE train_lora's os.environ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES clobber (sft.py:1005), freezing the driver device list at all-4-visible with CVD unset. The later clobber is silently ignored at the driver level while torch.cuda.is_initialized() stays False (the misleading part) and even device_count() returns 1 — but allocations to cuda:0 land on PHYSICAL GPU 0 for every process regardless of --gpu. Verified: (a) solo cell with --gpu 1 allocates on nvidia index 0; (b) tracer shows CVD='1' honored at torch-level lazy_init yet placement still phys 0; (c) minimal repro: script imports -> set CVD=1 -> allocate -> lands phys 0, while a clean process (no script imports) with the same late CVD set lands phys 1. Launcher template substitution + TrainLoraConfig.gpu_id flow verified correct.

Fix (launcher-level, no repo code change): pin CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<gpu> in the LAUNCHER environment per cell (before exec) while keeping --gpu <gpu>; the in-process clobber then rewrites the same value (no-op) and the early cuInit freeze happens under the correct 1-GPU visibility. Audited safe: train_lora device_map={'':0}, eval_issue543.py device='cuda:0' + same-value clobber at :584, dev-check/checkpoint-probe children inherit env. Re-dispatching experimenter with the fixed launcher (relaunch 3). Experimenter-respawn 1 of cap 3.
